why: I checked each verifier PASS/FAIL condition against the words of its expect line. Checks 1 and 2 stay within their lines. Their sample values only test left padding with fill, the default space, the target width and returning s unchanged. Check 3 asks for a heading plus a description for each export, which is a reasonable reading of "a section". Check 4 breaks the criterion. The expect line says only "npm test passes", which an exit code of 0 already shows. The PASS condition also requires that "the output shows `# fail 0`". That is an exact-wording requirement the words do not force. Newer versions of `node --test` use the spec reporter, which prints "ℹ fail 0", so a passing run could be marked FAIL. That stricter check belongs under Advisory, not in PASS.
